# File `logger.hpp`

Logging configuration, initialization, and stream-style logging interfaces.

```cpp
#include "utils/logger/logger.hpp"

LOGGER_MODULE("Scheduler");

int main() {
  const puc::logger::LoggerConf config{
      .global_level = puc::logger::LogLevel::INFO,
      .logfile = "puc.log",
  };
  LOGGER_INIT(config);

  Logger<INFO> << "Scheduler started";
  Logger<ERROR> << "Scheduler stopped unexpectedly";
}
```

### `LOGGER_INIT`

```cpp
#define LOGGER_INIT(config)
```

Initialize the process-wide logger.

Call this macro from the program entry point after constructing a [puc::logger::LoggerConf](structpuc_1_1logger_1_1_logger_conf.md).

**Parameters**

- `config` — Global logger configuration.

[Source](../../utils/logger/logger.hpp#L246)

<a id="symbol-utils_2logger_2logger_8hpp_1afe144fc32be52607c8eac7e98ecdbc8b"></a>

### `LOGGER_MODULE`

```cpp
#define LOGGER_MODULE(module_name)
```

Declare the logger module used by the current translation unit.

Invoke this macro once at namespace scope in each implementation file that logs messages. It declares the file-local Logger variable template and makes the DEBUG, INFO, WARN, and ERROR enumerators available to it.

```cpp
LOGGER_MODULE("Scheduler");

void run() {
  Logger<INFO> << "Scheduler started";
}
```

**Parameters**

- `module_name` — Name included in log lines from this translation unit.

[Source](../../utils/logger/logger.hpp#L266)
